discovery: Quantum control of macroscopic mechanical motion: cavity optomechanics and ground-state cooling of mechanical oscillators
motivation: The nominees showed that mechanical objects containing billions of atoms can be prepared, controlled and measured in the quantum regime. Cleland and co-workers cooled a micromechanical resonator to its ground state and exchanged single quanta with a superconducting qubit (2010). Kippenberg and Aspelmeyer established cavity optomechanics, demonstrating radiation-pressure sideband cooling, strong optomechanical coupling, and ground-state cooling of optically addressed resonators, later extended to entanglement, squeezing and quantum-limited position measurement at and beyond the standard quantum limit. Their work turned radiation-pressure back-action from a textbook limitation into a controllable resource. Its impact is broad: quantum-limited force and displacement sensing, microwave-to-optical transduction for quantum networks, levitated nanoparticles cooled to the ground state, and new tests of quantum mechanics at macroscopic scales. This is a fundamental discovery that has become an instrument used across physics.
